counter_semantics.existing_prefetch_reader_mean: HtpProfile.addPrefetchRead for the host bank begins inside readHostExpert callback after payload allocation. From-host arena promotion/free is excluded. Its mean cannot predict bank duration by count/readers.
counter_semantics.timeline_read_service_us: Sum of overlapping readOne elapsed durations, starting before claim lock/new[] and ending under completion lock. Includes allocation, first touch, reader callback, scheduler and lock waits.
counter_semantics.timing_eligibility: Runner mode=clean is only its preset. NNTR_MOE_IO_PROFILE=1 and clean_timing_sample=false exclude both diagnostic TPS values from clean performance comparisons.
counter_semantics.whole_process_io: HTP-QS2-IO totals also cover model initialization and 64 decode tokens; not used to derive initial bank or late prefill IO.

findings: No measured 55 ms startup idle opportunity. Stage64 is ready only 1.583 ms before the first safe transition.
The stage128 initial all-bank join exposes 24.329 ms of wait in this run. A larger bank is not automatically better even when average per-record service is lower.
Final cancel/join/residual-free is only 7 us at64 and 4 us at128. End-of-prefill bulk cleanup is no longer a >=5 ms opportunity in these eager-release runs.
Worker startup is 0.382/0.470 ms; all requested records are read and consumed, with no cancellation or failure.
Aggregate service nearly fills seven concurrent readOne windows; this says elapsed work overlaps, not that CPUs are saturated.
remaining_coverage_limit: No record-level or later-layer timestamps were added. Bank-ready slack does not prove every reader thread was idle throughout it. Source-only analysis does not justify changing bounded bank-join scheduling.
